intent: To illustrate that driving alone is the dominant mode of commuting to work for Americans.

units.meaning: Drive alone is the largest commuting mode, accounting for 76.3% of the total—over three-quarters.
accepted_routes: Drive alone accounts for 76.3% of commuting mode share.
76.3% of commuters drive alone to work.
Driving alone is the biggest slice at 76.3%, over three-quarters.
Drive alone is 76.3%, the dominant mode.
units.visual_evidence_rule: A chart mark for Drive alone must be labeled or directly readable as 76.3% and visually the largest slice/bar.
units.temporal_anchor: overwhelming majority of Americans get to work by driving alone
units.reviewer_question: Must the video explicitly show or state 76.3% for Drive alone, or is 'overwhelming majority' without the number acceptable?

units.meaning: All other commuting modes combined total only 23.7%, so drive alone at 76.3% is a majority and more than three times all other modes combined.
accepted_routes: Drive alone is 76.3%, while every other mode together is 23.7%.
Driving alone is more than three times all other modes combined, about 3.2x.
The remaining 23.7% is split across all other commuting modes.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must make the non-Drive-alone total readable or show all other slices/bars summing to about 23.7%, with Drive alone at 76.3%.
units.temporal_anchor: overwhelming majority of Americans get to work by driving alone
units.reviewer_question: Should the video be required to contrast Drive alone against all other modes combined, or is the 76.3% largest-slice fact enough?

units.meaning: Carpool is the second-largest commuting mode at 8.2%, far behind drive alone's 76.3%.
accepted_routes: Carpool is the next most common mode after driving alone, at 8.2%.
After Drive alone, carpooling is the second-largest mode with 8.2%.
Drive alone's nearest competitor is carpooling at 8.2%.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Carpool must be visually or textually identifiable as the second-largest category, with 8.2% visible/readable.
units.temporal_anchor: optional; if present, attach to the same 'driving alone' dominance clause
units.reviewer_question: Is the second-place mode, carpool at 8.2%, required to convey dominance, or is it optional context?

units.meaning: Drive alone is about 9.3 times as common as the next-largest mode, carpool, comparing 76.3% with 8.2%.
accepted_routes: Drive alone is about 9.3 times as common as carpooling.
The drive-alone share is more than nine times the carpool share.
Carpooling is 8.2% compared with 76.3% for driving alone, a roughly 9.3x gap.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Both Drive alone 76.3% and Carpool 8.2% must be visible/readable if this ratio is stated.
units.temporal_anchor: optional; if used, immediately follow the 'overwhelming majority ... driving alone' clause
units.reviewer_question: Should the video include the explicit ratio to the next-largest mode, or is that over-explaining the dominance?

units.meaning: Drive alone exceeds carpool by 68.1 percentage points, since 76.3% minus 8.2% equals 68.1 points.
accepted_routes: Drive alone leads carpool by 68.1 percentage points.
The gap between drive alone and carpool is 68.1 percentage points.
Drive alone is 68.1 points above the second-place carpool.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Drive alone 76.3% and Carpool 8.2% must both be visible/readable if this gap is stated.
units.temporal_anchor: optional; if used, part of the dominance comparison clause
units.reviewer_question: Is a percentage-point gap required, or is it redundant with the share and ranking facts?

optional_valid: Public transportation is 5.2% of commuting mode share.
Work at home is 5.1% of commuting mode share.
Walk is 2.5% of commuting mode share.
Bicycle is the smallest listed mode at 1.0%.
Taxi, motorcycle, or other is 1.7% of commuting mode share.
Public transportation, at 5.2%, is slightly above work at home, at 5.1%.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal claims such as driving alone is one reason for any outcome or why it is not ideal.
Extrapolating from the table to all Americans, all workers, or population counts not in the table.
Treating Drive alone 76.3% as a share of all Americans rather than of commuting mode share in this chart.
Claiming exact rankings without checking the table, such as public transportation being second.
Summing categories to something other than the table-consistent total or using the wrong denominator.
Separating Taxi or motorcycle as its own mode instead of the combined table category 'Taxi, motorcycle, or other'.
notes: The strongest required core is Drive alone as the largest share at 76.3%; the all-other-combined contrast is the clearest way to show dominance but may be optional depending on reviewer standards. Optional ranking and ratio units are included as trade-offs, not obligations.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
